4. Custom Fitting: MuSyC Synergy

gDR team

2026-11-04

4. Custom Fitting: MuSyC Synergy

gDR Analysis Pipeline

Date: 2026-11-04

Author: gDR team

1 Introduction

The gDR pipeline scores combinations with Bliss, HSA and the Loewe-based combination index (Step 3). This report shows how a different model is added on top of the same processed data without changing the pipeline: a fit function is passed to gDRutils::apply_fit(), which calls it once per drug pair, cell line and normalization type, and stores the results as a new assay next to the native ones.

The model here is MuSyC (multi-dimensional synergy of combinations, Meyer et al., Cell Systems 2019). It fits a dose-response surface to the whole combination grid and separates two kinds of synergy:

  • synergy of potency, alpha12 and alpha21: one drug shifts the potency of the other (alpha > 1 synergistic, alpha < 1 antagonistic);
  • synergy of efficacy, beta: the combination reaches a deeper maximal effect than the stronger drug alone (beta > 0 synergistic).

The fit function, gDRcore::musyc_fit_fn(), runs the fit in the Python synergy package through reticulate. Install it once with reticulate::py_install("synergy", pip = TRUE). It needs gDRcore 1.11.30 or later, which is not on Bioconductor yet: install gDRutils and gDRcore from GitHub with remotes::install_github(c("gdrplatform/gDRutils", "gdrplatform/gDRcore")).

library(qs2)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(data.table)
library(writexl)
library(gDRutils)
library(gDRcore)
library(gDRplots)
library(ggplot2)
if (packageVersion("gDRcore") < "1.11.30") {
  stop("This report needs gDRcore 1.11.30 or later: ",
       "remotes::install_github(c(\"gdrplatform/gDRutils\", \"gdrplatform/gDRcore\"))")
}
if (!musyc_available()) {
  stop("This report needs the Python 'synergy' package: reticulate::py_install(\"synergy\", pip = TRUE)")
}

2 Read the gDR MAE data

This report starts from the MultiAssayExperiment saved by Step 2 and uses its combination experiment.

wd <- getwd()
dir.create(file.path(wd, "tables"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
mae <- qs_read(file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_mae.qs2"))
combo_se <- mae[[get_supported_experiments("combo")]]
assayNames(combo_se)
## [1] "RawTreated"     "Controls"       "Normalized"     "Averaged"      
## [5] "Metrics"        "excess"         "isobolograms"   "all_iso_points"
## [9] "scores"

3 The fit function contract

A fit function receives the Averaged responses of one cell — one drug pair, one cell line, one normalization type — as a data.table with the two concentrations and the response x, and returns a named list. Every element becomes a column of the output assay.

cell_line_col <- get_env_identifiers("cellline_name")
drug_col <- get_env_identifiers("drug_name")
drug2_col <- get_env_identifiers("drug_name2")
id_cols <- c(cell_line_col, drug_col, drug2_col, "normalization_type")

avg_dt <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(combo_se, "Averaged")
one_cell <- avg_dt[avg_dt[[cell_line_col]] == avg_dt[[cell_line_col]][1] &
                     avg_dt[[drug_col]] == avg_dt[[drug_col]][1] &
                     normalization_type == "GR"]
head(one_cell[, c("Concentration", "Concentration_2", "x")])
##    Concentration Concentration_2       x
##            <num>           <num>   <num>
## 1:             0     0.000762079 1.00885
## 2:             0     0.002286236 1.05905
## 3:             0     0.006858703 1.04545
## 4:             0     0.020576144 0.75525
## 5:             0     0.061728397 0.42555
## 6:             0     0.185185083 0.31230
str(musyc_fit_fn(one_cell))
## List of 14
##  $ normalization_type: chr "GR"
##  $ E0                : num 1.01
##  $ E1                : num 0.719
##  $ E2                : num 0.241
##  $ E3                : num 0.24
##  $ h1                : num 7.54
##  $ h2                : num 1.69
##  $ C1                : num 0.138
##  $ C2                : num 0.0316
##  $ alpha12           : num 3.14
##  $ alpha21           : num 1.21
##  $ beta              : num 0.0011
##  $ r2                : num 0.928
##  $ converged         : logi TRUE

4 Fit MuSyC to every cell

apply_fit() runs the fit function over the whole SE. musyc_summary_fn() then collapses the fits of the two normalization types into one row per cell. Both results land next to the native assays; nothing that was there is changed.

combo_se <- apply_fit(
  combo_se,
  fit_fn = musyc_fit_fn,
  data_type = "combination",
  output_assay = "musyc_params",
  summary_fn = musyc_summary_fn,
  summary_assay = "musyc_summary",
  fit_source = "musyc"
)
assayNames(combo_se)
##  [1] "RawTreated"     "Controls"       "Normalized"     "Averaged"      
##  [5] "Metrics"        "excess"         "isobolograms"   "all_iso_points"
##  [9] "scores"         "musyc_params"   "musyc_summary"
musyc_params <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(combo_se, "musyc_params")
musyc_summary <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(combo_se, "musyc_summary")
clip_log2 <- function(v) pmin(pmax(log2(v), -10), 10)
musyc_params[, log2_alpha := (clip_log2(alpha12) + clip_log2(alpha21)) / 2]
param_cols <- c("E3", "h1", "h2", "C1", "C2", "alpha12", "alpha21", "log2_alpha", "beta", "r2", "converged")
musyc_gr <- musyc_params[normalization_type == "GR", c(id_cols, param_cols), with = FALSE]
generate_datatable(musyc_gr[, lapply(.SD, function(v) if (is.numeric(v)) signif(v, 3) else v)])

log2_alpha is the mean of log2(alpha12) and log2(alpha21), each clipped to [-10, 10] first, as in musyc_summary_fn(). 166 of 172 fits converged, with a median R² of 0.979. A fit that does not converge has NA parameters and is left out below.

5 Potency and efficacy synergy

Each point is one cell line and drug pair (GR). Points to the right show synergy of potency, points above zero synergy of efficacy.

musyc_gr <- musyc_gr[converged %in% TRUE]
musyc_gr[, pair := paste(get(drug_col), "x", get(drug2_col))]
ggplot(musyc_gr, aes(log2_alpha, beta, colour = pair)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "mean log2(alpha): synergy of potency", y = "beta: synergy of efficacy", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

alpha is estimated well only when the surface constrains it. Where the combination barely moves the response, very different alpha values fit the data equally well, so read alpha together with the dose-response surface and r2, not on its own.

6 MuSyC next to Bliss

The native scores assay holds the Bliss score of Step 3: one number for the excess over the independence expectation, whatever its cause. MuSyC splits that excess into potency and efficacy.

scores <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(combo_se, "scores")
compare <- merge(
  musyc_params[converged %in% TRUE, c(id_cols, "log2_alpha", "beta"), with = FALSE],
  scores[, c(id_cols, "bliss_score"), with = FALSE],
  by = id_cols
)
ggplot(compare, aes(bliss_score, beta)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~normalization_type) +
  labs(x = "Bliss score (Step 3)", y = "MuSyC beta") +
  theme_bw()

Of the 80 converged GR fits, Bliss is positive in 80. beta exceeds 0.1 (the dead zone of musyc_summary_fn()) in 21 of them, and log2(alpha) exceeds 1, at least a two-fold shift in potency, in 47. In these data the synergy comes mostly through potency — each drug makes the other work at lower doses — rather than through a deeper maximal effect. A single score such as Bliss cannot tell these apart.

7 MuSyC in the gDRplots combination plots

The MuSyC assay has the layout of the native scores assay — one row per drug pair, cell line and normalization type — so the gDRplots functions that draw the Bliss score in Step 3 draw any of its columns, log2_alpha included.

hm <- pheatmap_with_anno_combo(musyc_params, metric = "log2_alpha", fit_source = "musyc",
                               hm_title = "MuSyC mean log2(alpha), GR")
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(hm$heatmap$gtable)

plot_boxplot_metric_combo(musyc_params, group_var = cell_line_col, metric = "beta",
                          fit_source = "musyc", colored_pts_flag = TRUE)

8 Provenance

apply_fit() records how each assay was produced in the SE metadata, including the versions of the Python packages the MuSyC fit ran with, so the numbers can be traced back to the exact model.

summarize_fit_provenance(combo_se)
##             assay fit_source                                          fn
##            <char>     <char>                                      <char>
## 1:        Metrics        gDR      gDRcore::apply_combo_sa_fits (1.11.31)
## 2:         excess        gDR       gDRcore::apply_combo_excess (1.11.31)
## 3:   isobolograms        gDR gDRcore::apply_combo_isobolograms (1.11.31)
## 4: all_iso_points        gDR gDRcore::apply_combo_isobolograms (1.11.31)
## 5:         scores        gDR       gDRcore::apply_combo_scores (1.11.31)
## 6:   musyc_params      musyc             gDRcore::musyc_fit_fn (1.11.31)
## 7:  musyc_summary      musyc         gDRcore::musyc_summary_fn (1.11.31)
##                                                                                                                                                                                                                             fit_args
##                                                                                                                                                                                                                               <char>
## 1:                                                       series_identifiers = c("Concentration", "Concentration_2"), normalization_types = c("GR", "RV"), averaged_assay = "Averaged", metrics_assay = "Metrics", fit_source = "gDR"
## 2:                                                  series_identifiers = c("Concentration", "Concentration_2"), normalization_types = c("GR", "RV"), averaged_assay = "Averaged", metrics_assay = "Metrics", excess_assay = "excess"
## 3: series_identifiers = c("Concentration", "Concentration_2"), normalization_types = c("GR", "RV"), averaged_assay = "Averaged", metrics_assay = "Metrics", isobolograms_assay = "isobolograms", iso_points_assay = "all_iso_points"
## 4: series_identifiers = c("Concentration", "Concentration_2"), normalization_types = c("GR", "RV"), averaged_assay = "Averaged", metrics_assay = "Metrics", isobolograms_assay = "isobolograms", iso_points_assay = "all_iso_points"
## 5:                            scores_assay = "scores", averaged_assay = "Averaged", metrics_assay = "Metrics", excess_assay = "excess", normalization_types = c("GR", "RV"), fit_source = "gDR", isobolograms_assay = "isobolograms"
## 6:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
## 7:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
##                                                             model
##                                                            <char>
## 1: single-agent Hill fits along each axis of the combination grid
## 2:      HSA and Bliss excess over smoothed single-agent responses
## 3:                       Loewe isobolograms and combination index
## 4:                       Loewe isobolograms and combination index
## 5:           Bliss, HSA and CI scores per drug pair and cell line
## 6:              MuSyC (multi-dimensional synergy of combinations)
## 7:                                          MuSyC synergy summary
str(get_fit_provenance(combo_se, "musyc_params", "musyc")$fn$env)
## List of 4
##  $ python : chr "3.12"
##  $ synergy: chr "1.0.0"
##  $ numpy  : chr "2.5.4"
##  $ scipy  : chr "1.18.1"

9 Save the results

write_xlsx(
  list(musyc_params = musyc_params, musyc_summary = musyc_summary),
  file.path(wd, "tables", "musyc_params.xlsx")
)

10 Conclusion

A new model was fitted to the processed combination data by passing one function to apply_fit(). The same pattern applies to any model that maps the responses of one cell to a set of numbers: write the fit function, call apply_fit(), and the results travel with the data, provenance included.
